summary: End-of-prior-session and intraday reference levels captured for July 10, 2026.

headline: SK Hynix lists on Nasdaq in record ~$29B ADR offering, largest-ever U.S. share sale by a foreign company
summary: South Korea's SK Hynix began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under ticker SKHY on July 10, raising approximately $29 billion via American Depositary Shares—surpassing Alibaba and Saudi Aramco to become the largest-ever U.S. stock sale by a foreign firm. The ADR opened around $158, equivalent to ₩242,500 per domestic share with one common share split into 10 ADRs. The deal priced at ₩255,500 per share and was 7× oversubscribed.

KOSPI +4% on day, SK Hynix among winners

headline: Delta Air Lines Q2 2026: revenue $19.76B (+19%), EPS $2.44; net income fell 25% on higher fuel costs
summary: Delta Air Lines posted Q2 operating revenue of $19.76 billion, up 19% year-over-year, beating the $17.47B consensus estimate. Adjusted EPS came in at $2.44, above the $1.48 Street estimate. Net income dropped 25% to $1.6 billion amid elevated fuel costs, which the carrier said it expects to pass on to consumers. Delta affirmed its full-year guidance and forecast Q3 EPS of $2.00–$2.50.
key_facts: Net income $1.6B, down 25% YoY on higher fuel costs
CEO expects fares to stay firm despite fuel price slide
First major airline to report Q2 2026

headline: Levi Strauss Q2 revenue $1.56B (+8%), raises FY26 guidance; stock falls ~5% on weaker Q3 outlook
summary: Levi Strauss reported Q2 2026 net revenues of $1.56 billion (+8% YoY) and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.28, beating estimates. The company raised full-year revenue guidance to +7–7.5% and EPS to $1.46–$1.52. Despite the beat and raised dividend, shares fell roughly 5% in early trading as Q3 revenue growth guidance of 4–5% disappointed relative to Q2's 8% pace.
key_facts: Q3 revenue growth guided 4–5% vs Q2's 8%

headline: AstraZeneca stock drops ~9% after Wainua fails Phase III ATTR-CM heart trial
summary: AstraZeneca and Ionis Pharmaceuticals reported that Wainua (eplontersen) failed to meet its primary endpoint in the CARDIO-TTRansform Phase III trial, which evaluated the drug in 1,432 patients with ATTR-CM (transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy). Adding Wainua to standard care did not significantly reduce cardiovascular mortality or recurrent cardiac events over 140 weeks. AstraZeneca shares fell ~9%, erasing ~£23.3B in market cap—the stock's worst single-day drop since March 2020.
key_facts: Wainua failed primary composite endpoint of CV mortality + recurrent events
AZN stock -9%, worst day since March 2020
AZN lost ~£23.3B ($31.2B) in market cap at day low
Ionis/AZN still retain approved ATTR-PN indication for Wainua

headline: Alnylam +16%, BridgeBio +16% as rival Wainua fails ATTR-CM trial; Raymond James raises ALNY target to $468
summary: Alnylam Pharmaceuticals (ALNY) surged ~16–18% and BridgeBio Pharma (BBIO) climbed ~16% in premarket trading after AstraZeneca/Ionis' Wainua failed its Phase III heart disease trial, strengthening the competitive moat for Alnylam's ATTR silencer franchise (vutrisiran/Amvuttra). Raymond James raised its ALNY price target from $420 to $468, citing improved competitive positioning and potential pricing power.
key_facts: Wainua failure removes key competitor in ATTR-CM space

headline: Micron Technology surges 5% on AI memory demand; stock at $991, up 200%+ YTD
summary: Micron Technology (MU) shares rose ~5% to approximately $991.64 on July 10, driven by continued strong AI-driven demand for HBM and DRAM. Micron reported Q3 revenue of $41.5 billion (+346% YoY) with ~85% gross margin and guides Q4 revenue to $50B. Micron also announced a strategic AI memory supply partnership with Anthropic and a $3B domestic chip factory investment. Consensus target sits at $1,486 with a Strong Buy rating.

headline: Philadelphia Semiconductor Index +75% YTD despite recent 10.8% pullback; AI chip stocks add $2T in Q2
summary: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) gained roughly 75% year-to-date through early July 2026, adding a combined ~$2 trillion in market value across AI chip names during Q2—the index's best quarter on record (+87.8%). headline: Prologis pushes SEGRO board for talks on hostile £12.6B ($16.9B) all-share takeover bid
summary: Prologis (PLD), the world's largest industrial REIT, launched a hostile all-share bid for UK logistics giant SEGRO at £12.6 billion (~$16.9B), offering 0.084 new PLD shares per SEGRO share at a 24.6% premium to SEGRO's pre-announcement price of 742p. SEGRO's board rejected the offer as 'inadequate', but major SEGRO shareholders are urging engagement. Prologis has until July 22 to announce a firm intention or walk away.

Ultra Maritime is being sold by private equity firm Cobham Ultra (Advent). The acquired unit will join Lockheed's Rotary and Mission Systems business upon close.

headline: Kroger to acquire Giant Eagle for $1.65B, first major grocery deal since failed Albertsons merger
summary: Kroger announced a definitive agreement to buy family-owned Giant Eagle for $1.65 billion ($1.25B cash + ~$400M assumed liabilities), adding 197 supermarkets and 11 pharmacies across the Midwest and Mid-Atlantic. Giant Eagle generates ~$9B in annual sales. This is Kroger's first major acquisition since its $25B Albertsons deal collapsed in 2024. The deal is expected to close in 2027 and be accretive to earnings in the second full year after close.

headline: Strait of Hormuz shipping grinds to halt as US-Iran fighting resumes; no large vessel crossing since Tuesday
summary: Following renewed US military strikes on Iran and retaliatory attacks on tankers—including the LNG carrier Al Rekayat and supertanker Wedyan struck in the Strait of Hormuz on July 7—no large vessel has crossed the strait via the US-coordinated route while broadcasting its location since Tuesday July 8. Traceable crossings via the Oman-hugging lane have also effectively halted, sharply tightening global oil supply expectations.

The committee cited Iran conflict-driven oil prices, tariffs, and the AI investment boom as potential inflationary forces that could warrant tightening later in 2026. The June SEP raised the 2026 PCE inflation forecast to 3.6%.

headline: Semiconductors just had their best quarter ever: PHLX +87.8% in Q2, adding $2T in market cap
summary: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (PHLX) rose 87.8% in Q2 2026—the largest quarterly gain in records stretching back to 1994—as AI infrastructure spending by hyperscalers (Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta) drove unprecedented demand for advanced GPUs and memory chips. The index added approximately $2 trillion in combined market cap during the quarter.

headline: Lockheed Martin $3.5B Ultra Maritime deal expands sonar, sonobuoy and autonomous undersea warfare portfolio
summary: Lockheed Martin's $3.45 billion acquisition of Ultra Maritime Solutions (announced July 6) bolsters its undersea warfare capabilities with sonar systems, sonobuoys, torpedo defense, and autonomous maritime sensors. Ultra Maritime has an international footprint with exportable ASW products compatible with next-generation naval platforms. The unit is expected to integrate into Lockheed's Rotary and Mission Systems business.

headline: EIA July 2026 STEO: Brent forecast $74/b in Q3, down from $85 June average as Hormuz hopes partially offset Iran flare-up
summary: The EIA's July 2026 Short-Term Energy Outlook projects Brent crude to average $74 per barrel in Q3 2026, down from the June average of $85/b. The forecast embeds the expectation that Iranian output will partially recover after the June MOU, offset by renewed July Hormuz disruption risk. Production returning to near pre-conflict averages is projected by year-end 2026.

Iranian output expected to partially recover by year-end

headline: Trump says Iran reached out seeking negotiations; oil eases, risk appetite improves heading into July 10
summary: President Trump said on July 9 that Iran had reached out seeking diplomatic negotiations, while Qatar and Pakistan continued mediation efforts. The statement prompted a modest cooling in oil prices and an improvement in risk sentiment ahead of the July 10 open, with US stocks gaining into the close and Asian markets rising overnight.
